Before the Breach: Exploitation Prediction Matrix

Which newly published vulnerabilities attackers are most likely to use next, ranked only from what was known at each CVE's snapshot month, with the reasons and evidence behind each rank.

1

The problem

Tens of thousands of new vulnerabilities a year, and attackers use a tiny fraction. Security teams have to guess which ones to fix first.

2

The trap we found: NIST's data gives away the answer

NIST reviews attacked vulnerabilities first. So its own fields, read today, quietly reveal which old CVEs were exploited. A model trained on them looks brilliant in testing, then fails on new CVEs that haven't been reviewed yet. We removed every field like this, and verify.py re-proves the leak on every run.

3

Standard tools are blind on day one

Exploit code and EPSS are the usual early warnings. For most attacked CVEs, neither had fired by the end of the month they were published.

4

What a bug is says more than its severity score

How much more (or less) likely a 2024–25 CVE was to be exploited, by what its description says and who reported it. 1× = the average CVE.

5

Proof: it would have worked last year

Trained only on 2024 and tested on every CVE published January–September 2025, using only what was known at the end of each CVE's publish month, then checked against CISA's exploited list.

What does this mean for your team? Set your patch budget
Each month of 2025, a team patches the top N new CVEs by each method. How many of the CVEs CISA later confirmed as exploited would each method have caught?
Jan–Sep 2025 replay, trained on 2024 only. Ranks are within each month's new CVEs, using only what was known at the end of that month.

What the 2024–25 data says

Predictions, not confirmations: no CVE listed here was on CISA's KEV list at its snapshot. Ranks use no NIST-analysis fields (see COLUMNS_USED.md). Granite text is shown only when it passed the grounding validator. "Looks like" compares descriptions with KEV entries that were already listed at the CVE's snapshot.
